To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RWA mounds are abundant and continuously established in a managed Rhodope mountain forest, despite forestry practices, and tourism-related trampling loads.

(i) RWA mounds are more abundant than previously thought in Greek managed forests, (ii) RWA colonies can be found in areas with high trampling load and (iii) single-tree selection forestry practices are the most suitable for the conservation of RWA in the study area.
RWA are distributed throughout the forest and that their mounds are established in a variety of microhabitats.

the importance of forest management practices and the necessity of preserving RWA mounds for the maintenance of RWA populations.

the management of forests for RWA conservation should be based on the creation of a mosaic of microhabitats with different ages of trees and a variety of microclimates, which are necessary for the RWA to survive.

The main takeaway from our work is that
